senses.sense_definition: Having a lively, volatile, or unpredictable character; subject to sudden changes of mood or mind.

examples.text: His <w>mercurial</w> temperament made it very difficult for his coworkers to anticipate how he would react to feedback.
The manager had a notoriously <w>mercurial</w> nature, alternating between great enthusiasm and sudden anger without warning.

senses.sense_definition: Containing, consisting of, or caused by the chemical element mercury.

examples.text: The laboratory decided to replace every <w>mercurial</w> thermometer with a modern digital sensor to improve safety.
Workers exposed to high levels of the vapor suffered from severe <w>mercurial</w> poisoning.

senses.sense_definition: Pertaining to or characteristic of the planet Mercury.

examples.text: Astronomers gathered data to study the strange variations across the <w>mercurial</w> landscape.
The robotic probe endured intense solar radiation while analyzing the thin <w>mercurial</w> atmosphere.

senses.sense_definition: Pertaining to the Roman god Mercury; crafty, shrewd, or skilled in trade.

examples.text: He wielded a <w>mercurial</w> cunning that allowed him to outsmart rival merchants at every turn.
The ancient poet praised the traveler for his <w>mercurial</w> eloquence and swift feet.

senses.sense_definition: Pertaining to the astrological influence of the planet Mercury.

examples.text: The ancient astrologer claimed that the child possessed a distinctly <w>mercurial</w> intellect due to the alignment of the stars.
According to the chart, those under a strong <w>mercurial</w> influence are naturally drawn toward scholarship and debate.

senses.sense_definition: Caused by the medicinal or toxic action of mercury.

examples.text: The historical medical treatise documented several cases of painful <w>mercurial</w> ulceration in treated patients.
Frequent administration of the compound induced a violent <w>mercurial</w> tremor in the patient.

senses.sense_definition: A chemical compound or preparation containing mercury.

examples.text: The chemist carefully examined the hazardous <w>mercurial</w> before sealing it in a glass container.
Historically, doctors frequently administered a powerful <w>mercurial</w> to treat infectious diseases.

senses.sense_definition: A person who is volatile, quick-witted, or born under the astrological influence of Mercury.

examples.text: The young actor was such a <w>mercurial</w> that no one could predict how he would perform from one night to the next.
Known as a clever <w>mercurial</w>, he always found an ingenious way to wriggle out of trouble.

senses.sense_definition: Any plant belonging to the genus Mercurialis.

examples.text: The botanist catalogued a wild <w>mercurial</w> growing among the stones near the forest path.
Farmers often weeded out the common <w>mercurial</w> because it spread aggressively across the cultivated field.
